seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. What Zoom Workplace names. Read the company and the product family as two layers. Wikipedia describes Zoom Communications, Inc., formerly Zoom Video Communications, Inc., founded in 2011 by Eric Yuan, with the software launched in January 2013. That history is not a dial plan. It tells you which company publishes the pages you are about to trust.
seeds.eg: Wikipedia's article, opened as Zoom Communications, calls the company a communications technology company in San Jose, known primarily for the videoconferencing platform Zoom.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Zoom Phone developer paths. The page says you can integrate communication features into apps, including contact center workflows and CRM calling, automate voicemail handling and call processing, and manage users and devices programmatically. Those are job names, not a configuration export from a tenant.
seeds.eg: The Zoom Phone developer page is written for admins who set up Zoom Phone and for developers who build apps.

seeds.ti: Zoom API access, one hour at a time
seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Zoom API access, one hour at a time. Account-wide automation and a user-consented app are different grants. The page says OAuth uses an authorization code that you exchange for a token, and server-to-server OAuth uses app credentials to request a token directly. Refresh the user token, or request a new server-to-server token, when the hour ends.
seeds.eg: The API reference says to obtain an access token with OAuth or server-to-server authentication.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Agents and consumers. A contact center, in the Wikipedia article that opened, extends a call centre with channels beyond voice. Zoom's developer page is more specific for this product: voice, video, or chat, and two roles. Write the role before you write the channel. A chat from a consumer is not an agent-to-agent meeting just because both can use Zoom.
seeds.eg: The Contact Center developer page separates agents from consumers.

seeds.ti: Three ways to put Contact Center in an app
seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Three ways to put Contact Center in an app. Read the best-for line before you pick a kit. Smart Embed keeps the agent in one internal app. The SDK is the path when you need more than a softphone and you will own the interface. A desktop Zoom App stays inside Zoom.
seeds.eg: Smart Embed places the agent UI in a web app, with little code, for internal tools.

seeds.ti: Zoom Virtual Agent, and the license line
seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Zoom Virtual Agent, and the license line. Virtual Agent is a Zoom CX name. The guide you opened is a developer guide for deploying chat, not a staffing model. People and the virtual agent can both be called agents. Write virtual when you mean the SDK.
seeds.eg: The Virtual Agent developer guide shows an SDK for web, Android, and iOS.

seeds.ti: Talkdesk as a cloud contact center
seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Talkdesk as a cloud contact center. Use the titles you opened. Talkdesk presents itself as contact center software. This lab does not add a founding year, a headquarters, or a valuation, because those were not on a Talkdesk page or a Wikipedia article that opened. A search snippet mentioned Talkdesk on other Wikipedia pages. Snippets are not the article.
seeds.eg: The Talkdesk home page title that opened calls it contact center software and AI customer experience automation.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Talkdesk OAuth, account or user. Choose the grant from the audience. A customer automating their own instance is the Client Credentials case the page describes. An AppConnect partner signing a user in is the Authorization Code case. The page also names Signed JWT in the documentation index beside those grants. This room quotes the two grants the authentication page's opening table defines.
seeds.eg: The authentication page says Talkdesk supports OAuth 2.0.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Connections, contacts, and agents. Synchronization names tell you the direction of the study question. Contact Synchronization is about contacts. seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. What SIP is for. Signaling and media are different jobs. SIP, in the RFC that opened, sets up the session. RTP, in RFC 3550, is the transport protocol for real-time applications. If you debug a dial tone by staring at an RTP port, you may be in the wrong job.
seeds.eg: RFC 3261 is an application-layer control protocol for creating, modifying, and terminating sessions.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Offer, answer, and SDP. RFC 3261 says the invitation carries session descriptions so the parties can agree on media types. RFC 3264 is the model for that agreement. Read the offer and the answer as a pair. An answer that invents a codec the offer never listed is not the model those RFCs describe.
seeds.eg: RFC 3264 defines an offer/answer model that uses SDP.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Part of this note is unconfirmed. RTP, SRTP, and delay words. Media quality is a budget of delay, loss, and codec. This lab will not state a millisecond limit it did not read. G.114 is the recommendation to open when someone says the call feels late. G.711 is the PCM recommendation to open when someone says the codec is G.711.
seeds.eg: RFC 3550 is RTP, a transport protocol for real-time applications.

seeds.ti: A ladder you are allowed to draw
seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. A ladder you are allowed to draw. The honest ladder for this lab has a caller, a SIP element that can proxy or register, and a called party. The arrows you can name from the pages that opened are the session setup and the registration function. Label anything else as a sketch and point at the RFC section you still need.
seeds.eg: A ladder is a drawing of messages between named boxes.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Routing words that survived contact. Routing is the decision that picks a destination. CTI is the coordination between the telephone and the computer, including screen pop as a desktop idea on the Wikipedia page. A screen pop is not the route. It is what the desktop does when the route has already chosen an agent.
seeds.eg: Wikipedia's CTI article says the term covers desktop efficiency and server functions such as automatic call routing.

seeds.ti: Transfer, conference, and what stays confirm
seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Part of this note is unconfirmed. Transfer, conference, and what stays confirm. Students expect a transfer ladder. The honest version is short. Modifying a session is in the SIP abstract. The method name and the success responses belong to a section this session did not quote. Draw a box labeled modify, and a confirm row for the method.
seeds.eg: RFC 3261 includes modifying a session, not only creating one.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Workforce management, the general word. WFM is not one vendor's screen. The Wikipedia article is the general word: forecasting and scheduling sit inside a larger workforce process. Zoom lists the module. Talkdesk documents import APIs for schedules and forecasts. Avaya's opened pages did not use the letters WFM in the extracted lines. Do not invent an Avaya WFM module.
seeds.eg: Wikipedia defines workforce management as a process to optimize productivity, competency, and engagement.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Part of this note is unconfirmed. Talkdesk schedule and forecast imports. Both pages say the API is part of the Talkdesk Workforce Management product. Both pages have a subscription limits section. This session did not copy the numeric limits. Write confirm for any cap.
seeds.eg: The Schedule Event Import API uploads agent schedule events into Talkdesk WFM with CSV files.

seeds.ex: Checked 2026-10. Recording architecture and quality scores. A recording file is the copy of the media. A quality score is a review of a call. Zoom's navigation lists Quality Management next to Contact Center. That is a product name, not the RFC. Talkdesk's opened pages did not define a QM score formula. Avaya's AI Insights line says measure outcomes and does not define a score.
seeds.eg: RFC 7245 describes architectures for recording media with SIP, including call centers.

docs.eg: Wikipedia's Enhanced 911 article says E911 provides the caller's location to 911 dispatchers in North America.

docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. Analytics names, not fake charts. Analytics is where study notes usually go wrong, because a bar looks like a measurement. If the number is not on a page you opened, the bar is decoration and must be labeled that way. This lab's charts count rooms, tracks, and names that appeared in navigation.
docs.eg: Zoom's Contact Center navigation lists CX Insights and Analytics and reporting as labels on the product page.

docs.ti: Numbers you may repeat, and numbers you may not
docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. Part of this note is unconfirmed. Numbers you may repeat, and numbers you may not. A number is allowed in this lab only when you can point at the page. The four numbers above have pages. A fifth number that feels familiar, such as a well-known delay budget, stays confirm because it was not on the text that was read.
docs.eg: Zoom's API sample shows expires_in 3599, and the prose says tokens are valid for one hour.

docs.ti: CRM calling on the Zoom Phone page
docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. CRM calling on the Zoom Phone page. CRM integration here means the phone event and the customer record meet. The Zoom page says you can integrate CRM calling. It does not name a CRM product in the sentences that were read. Write the CRM name only after you open that CRM's page or your own admin screen.
docs.eg: The Zoom Phone developer page names CRM calling as an integration example.

docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. Talkdesk contact and agent sync. A real integration, in the sense this lab can defend, is a named API. Talkdesk names contact sync, agent sync, and a schedule import from an HRIS-style tool. Those are three integrations. A customer logo is not required to study them, and none was opened.
docs.eg: The docs index lists Contact Synchronization and Agent Synchronization.

docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. AI agents across three vendors. An AI agent in a contact center can mean a virtual responder, an assistant beside a human, or a navigation label. Write which one. Zoom's virtual agent guide is a chat SDK. Avaya's Tandem Care sentence is shared context between humans and AI. Talkdesk's title is a company positioning line. They are not one architecture.
docs.eg: Zoom Virtual Agent has a developer SDK for chat on web, Android, and iOS.

docs.ti: A migration habit that does not invent a cutover
docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. A migration habit that does not invent a cutover. Study migrations as a reversible change to one number. Save the old route, test the new route, and keep a way back. That habit is how you avoid a one-way Saturday. It is not a quote from a Zoom or Avaya runbook, because those runbooks were not opened.
docs.eg: Avaya's own line says to use AI to understand existing workflows and move to Infinity faster.

docs.ti: Leaving Aura or moving toward Infinity
docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. Leaving Aura or moving toward Infinity. A move that starts on Aura can be a voice move, a contact-center move, or both. The pages you opened do not say those move together. Ask which product the numbers live on.
docs.eg: Aura remains the enterprise voice and UC name on its page.

docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. Part of this note is unconfirmed. Licenses the pages actually name. License study starts with the sentence that names the license. There is one clear sentence in this set: the Zoom Virtual Agent license for Android and iOS SDKs. Everything else people call a license, a seat, or a bundle is confirm until the pricing or admin page is opened.
docs.eg: Zoom Virtual Agent's guide says Android and iOS SDKs require a Zoom Virtual Agent license.

docs.ti: Certifications you still have to open
docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. Certifications you still have to open. Say certification only with a noun. An app can be certified for a marketplace. A person can hold a credential. This session opened an index line about partner app certification on Talkdesk, and a link named Avaya Learning. It did not open a human exam blueprint for Zoom, Talkdesk, or Avaya.
docs.eg: Avaya Documentation links to Avaya Learning.

docs.ti: Roadmap, timelines, and the check date
docs.ex: Checked 2026-10. Roadmap, timelines, and the check date. Timelines in a study lab rot. The honest timeline is the date you opened the page. Write last checked 2026-10 on every source row. When a page carries its own date, copy that date and say what it dates: a markdown file, or a registry.
docs.eg: Every citation in this lab was checked in October 2026.
